u0: The normal progress state: no immediate pickup obligation from a fall is outstanding. You still must be carrying the box when you reach the exit, and every future fall must be answered by holding the box on the immediately following step. Reaching the exit while empty-handed leaves the carrying condition open, while reaching it with the box satisfies that condition; ordinary movement and waiting are allowed while nothing is pending.
u1: A fall has just occurred, so the box is not in your hands and the immediate recovery requirement is active. On the very next step you must be holding the box again; doing so clears the obligation and returns you to normal progress. If you are still not holding it on that step, the mandatory next-step pickup has been missed and the attempt is failed.
u2: The exit has been reached without the box in hand, and no fall occurred on that step, so the exit-carrying condition is still open. If you come to hold the box on a later step without a new fall, the condition clears and normal progress resumes. While you remain empty-handed and no fall happens, this state simply waits; a fall while you are not holding the box moves you into a stricter immediate-recovery situation.
u3: This state records a fall that left the box out of your hands while the exit-carrying condition is also unresolved, so both the immediate pickup and the carrying-at-exit requirements are pending. The very next step must leave you holding the box; if it does, normal progress resumes and the pending conditions are cleared. If you are still empty-handed on that next step, the attempt fails permanently. Waiting is not safe in this state.
u4: The required immediate pickup after a fall was missed: the box was not back in your hands on the immediately following step, or an already-pending recovery was left unfulfilled. This violates a mandatory requirement, so successful completion is no longer possible and the failure is irreversible.
